column1: # The corpus. One design per line, tab-separated. Its card is the .card file beside it.
#   path    the verdict it must get    what `petra check` gives today, if wrong    what the kernel gives today, if wrong    why
# corpus/run.py explains the verdicts and what fails a run.
# Where the expected verdicts come from:
#   examples/            what the example's name or header says it shows. For the passing
#                        steel and electronics examples that is the verdict they ship with,
#                        which nothing outside Petra has confirmed.
#   judges/canaries/     each is a design the outside judge rejects, so it must not pass.
#   corpus/cases/pilot/  designs from the lift pilot that the steel tests reason about.
#   corpus/cases/audit/  the audit of 2026-11-09. "re-ran" means the lead auditor reproduced
#                        the verdict, "auditor" that one auditor reported it. A design the
#                        type rules refuse must be an INPUT_ERROR.
#                        A waiver there is one the designer wrote, so it is in the design
#                        file, where the language refuses it.
#   corpus/cases/found/  designs found while fixing others. The note says what each showed.
#   audit F1 to F4       false FAILs whose truth is the auditor's memory of Manual tables.
#   hook_uncertain       the audit disputes its PASS by analysis, with no run.
#   examples/families/   inputs to `petra certify-family`, not to `petra check`.
#   three weld_bracket_support_side canaries, which FAIL after about 150 s, past the limit.
